title: Cohort-shingle sampler: token-length-aware exemplar packs for quant calibration
creator: Lina Chen
description: Goal: produce representative, compact calibration packs for FP8/INT8 quant profiles that maximize accuracy preservation on production prompt distributions while minimizing calibration compute and preserving tenant privacy. We will introduce a cohort-shingle sampler that constructs per-cohort exemplar packs using token-length bucketing, shingled n-gram novelty scoring, and soft tenant-weighting so low-volume but high-impact cohorts are not lost. Packs will include holdout subsets for validation and be compatible with existing calibration runners (int8/fp8) and our evaluation harness. This ticket covers algorithm design, implementation in the sampler service, integration with the calibration pipeline, and verification against production holdouts.
acceptance_criteria: Sampler produces per-cohort packs of target size with stable composition across repeated runs (variance < 5% on key cohort heuristics)
Calibration using generated packs yields <= 1.0% drop in production-norm accuracy (as measured by per-task BLEU/F1/QA-EM where applicable) relative to full-sample baseline for FP8 and INT8 profiles
Holdout validation set (30% of cohort pack) must detect a regression >= 1.5% with >80% power (simulated via bootstrapped evaluation)
Output artifacts are annotated with provenance (cohort id, sampling seed, token-length distribution) and stored in the calibration bucket with access controls
Sampler respects tenant opt-outs and redacts PII per privacy policy; security review completed and docs updated
implementation_notes: Introduce token-length buckets (e.g., 0-64, 65-256, 257-1024) per cohort; enforce minimum representation from each bucket to preserve sequence-length sensitivity for kernel selection

Compute shingle novelty score per prompt: weighted combination of n-gram rarity (in cohort corpus) and recency; use reservoir sampling within novelty-deciles to keep headroom for rare but relevant prompts
Soft tenant-weighting: upweight low-volume tenants by a capped multiplier to avoid domination by a handful of high-volume customers; weight table stored in metadata service
Construct packs with stratified holdouts (e.g., 70/30 split) ensuring holdout mirrors bucket & novelty distributions
Provide a lightweight synthetic augmentation pass for cohorts under min_size (theta augmentation using paraphrase templates + temperature sampling), flagged in metadata
Expose sampler as a job in calibration-orchestration with stable seed and dry-run mode; results written to s3 path /calibration-packs/{release}/{cohort}/{seed}/pack.jsonl
Add authorization checks and encryption-at-rest for exported packs; coordinate with Security for KMS key usage
test_plan: Unit tests for bucket assignment, shingle scoring, and reservoir selection with deterministic seeds
Integration test: run sampler against recent 7-day traffic snapshot and validate distribution metrics (token-length, novelty quantiles) vs production distribution within tolerance
E2E calibration run: generate packs for 10 representative cohorts, run INT8 and FP8 calibration pipelines, compare model outputs on holdouts vs baseline (unquantized) using task-specific metrics
A/B validation: route 10% of production inference to models calibrated with new packs for 48h (shadow mode) and collect regression signals; stop on high-severity regressions
Privacy test: assert redaction pipeline removes PII tokens and confirm with synthetic PII injection tests
metrics: pack_size_bytes: target <= 50MB per pack for cohorts > 10k prompts
risks: Overweighting rare tenants may produce packs that underrepresent majority traffic causes unexpected regressions
Synthetic augmentation could introduce unnatural artifacts that bias calibration if not flagged
Privacy/token-redaction edge cases may leak signal into calibration if not exhaustively validated
Sampler complexity increases runtime and might delay calibration cadence; need to monitor generation_time_per_cohort
rollout_steps: 1) Merge sampler implementation behind feature flag with dry-run outputs to test bucket & novelty stats (week 1)
2) Generate packs for 20 held-out cohorts and run internal FP8/INT8 calibration runs (week 2)
3) Run shadow A/B calibration of models produced with new packs on non-customer traffic and monitor metrics for 72h (week 3)
4) Coordinate security sign-off and opt-out migration for tenant privacy flags (week 4)
5) Enable production generation for low-risk cohorts and incrementally expand contingent on metrics (week 5+)
6) Post-release audit: collect calibration performance dashboard for 30 days and produce a runbook for pack regeneration cadence
